lines.en: I open up the door to Ami’s room and, lo and behold, she’s not inside. Though, I probably could have predicted that on account of it being far too convenient.
We’ve yet to check my house though, so I do my best to be helpful and suggest it to Himawari once she gets off the phone with who I presume is that Shiori girl.
But when she agrees straightaway, I’m suddenly stricken with an odd bout of nervousness at the thought of introducing her to my other home. The one without her.
And I shouldn’t be given that she’s seen it a million times before (albeit via divine spycam), but it doesn’t change anything.
I just don’t want her comparing what I have now to what I might have one day if I play my cards right.
Not because I think she’ll be jealous, though. Or that she’ll wish she could be the one there with me, which I know she’ll do regardless.
But because I think it might make her sad. Or lonely when she thinks back on it when this all blows over.
I know I will — and she must take after me in some way. So all I can really do is hope that those moments in which she is most purely my daughter don’t come when the cameras are off.
But then again, I hope for her sake that they’re never on at all.
We check the house and find nothing.
We check the school and find nothing.
We check the maid cafe and the market in our neighborhood and even the newly renovated mall and still we find nothing.
Just how far could she have gone? And how did she go at all?
Because I might not see Ami the same exact way I see Himawari, but that doesn’t mean the idea of her facing something as terrifying as this alone doesn’t break my heart.
And if she’s been doing that all along?...Facing these catastrophes on her own while I fraternize in tents with her best friend?...
If she’s been doing that, what can I even say to her?
: Hah...
: I take it this is what you meant when you said Ami can be “troublesome” sometimes?
: Not exactly...but you’re not entirely wrong either. She just makes damn sure that this is always as difficult as possible for us.
: So, in the event that we can’t find her, what happens then?
: The same thing that’s been happening to you and Mom and now Makoto, I guess. She’ll keep all of her memories intact and move onto the next cycle without any reformatting.
: Oh...Well, isn’t that a good thing? Wouldn’t we want her to do that since it’d give us more of a foothold in trying to escape these loops once and for all?
: It’s bad for a number of reasons. But before I bother elaborating, do you even think that Ami would want to leave a place like this?
: Because this is sort of like her Aomori, isn’t it? A world where she can spend every waking moment with the person she loves the most?
: Maybe...
: But if this is Maya’s wish, it means that Ami likely already has some place like that.
: And that there’s another her and another me there right now, happily coexisting without the fear and pain and everything else we’ve grown used to here.
: So even if she doesn’t want to leave this place, it wouldn’t be right to just...keel over and let whatever is going to happen actually happen.
: Especially not if it’s going to put my life with you at risk.
: ...What? Why are you looking at me like that?
: I’m just proud to hear you finally talking like you understand your purpose.
: It’s been tough, you know...Watching you say so many terrible things about yourself from behind a screen. Wanting to help but knowing I can’t.
: If I wasn’t so brave and strong, this might even be the scene where I jump into your arms and start crying about not wanting to leave again.
: Do you ever cry? Because I can’t really imagine it. Or do you just take after your mother and do it in private?
: That’s for me to know and you to never find out. But I’ll tell you this — if I was going to cry, I definitely wouldn’t do it while you’re still here.
: Don’t want your final moments with me to be spoiled by the fact that you’d have to keep handing me tissues. Banter like this is much healthier.
: I don’t mind being your tissue dispenser if I have to. Comes with the territory, probably. I don’t know. I only have a few months of experience when it comes to being an actual father.
: It was a great few months, though...wasn’t it?
: It was...
: Maybe don’t check your phone for a few months after this, though. I’m probably going to be in even worse shape than Ayane once you’re gone.
: You’ll be fine. Don’t worry. I know you’ll figure things out even when I’m not there to guide you.
: Well, I’m glad you have faith in me, at least.
: It’s much easier to have faith when you know how everything ends.
: Yet here you are, breaking every single rule your weird god-company has in order to validate that faith. Why not just let it all play out and trust the process if you’re so sure?
: Because, despite my status as the bravest and cutest time-travelling magical girl to ever set foot in Kumon-mi, I’m still just an annoying teenager who loves her parents too much for her own good.
: That said, you should probably hurry up and escape this terrible fate so I stop making bad decisions. I require guidance you can not provide from this dimension.
: I’ll do what I can...
: I just hope that knowing you’re out there watching over us doesn’t influence my actions too much. Because there are a lot of girls who might murder me if I stop giving them attention.
: Speaking of which, I still haven’t told you about Ami. And why you probably don’t want her memories carrying over.
: You’re not going to tell me she’s a wish too, are you? Because that would probably make these last twenty-four hours the most depressingly consequential of my entire life.
: I’m pretty sure they already were before we even got to the Ami stuff. But no. She’s real.
: She’s different though.
: Different...how?
: Different because-
: Because she knows.
: Ayane?...
: How did you even-
: I don’t know...
: I passed out from crying too hard and I was here when I woke up...
: My head hurts...My eyes hurt...I want to curl up into a ball and die...
: I miss Aomori...And I don’t know if I’m going to be okay this time...
: But maybe...
: For the next few hours...
: I can pretend I am?...
: Y-You don’t have to pretend anything! It’s my fault you’re upset in the first place! I took everything from you in a single moment! Being upset just means that you-
: Hima-chan...was I a good mother?
: What?...Of course you were. How can you even ask that?
: I’ve always wanted to be a mom...Like, that was my dream. Having a family. Coming home to the same faces every day. Waking up to them in the morning.
: I had that once when I was little. It felt like the whole world was confined to things that happened in my house. And that everything else was just noise.
: But one day, it all went away. And all I had left was noise.
: The house was quiet when I woke up. There was no conversation when I’d go to the kitchen because there was no one home but me.
: I never realized just how loud everything can be when there’s nothing there to distract you.
: The water in the pipes...the hum of the air conditioner in summer...
: The wind chime my mother bought that I used to love before its sound became a plague on my ears that did nothing but remind me she was gone.
: I even grew to despise the sound of the birds because I needed to be mad at something and there was just nothing else to be mad at.
: I always told myself I would never let something like that happen. That my children would never have to feel alone and would never wake up to an empty home like I did.
: That I would always be there for them no matter how bad things got. And that they’d be able to count on me even if it felt like they couldn’t.
: I have never been more hurt than I am right now. I feel like a piece of me has been ripped out and torn to shreds. That my lungs are full of fire and my heart is collapsing.
: But even if it was you who made me feel that way, it’s you who lets me feel at all.
: Mom-
: I won’t let you hate the birds as well.
: You are still Hima-chan...and I am still your mother.
: I am sorry I made you feel alone.
: No, it’s...
: I haven’t felt alone. Dad’s been with me. And I...fully expected you to hurt like this, so...if anything, you should be scolding me for intentionally putting you through that.
: I’m the one who should be apologizing. Not you.
: You never have to apologize to me, Hima-chan.
: No, there should definitely be a clause in there that allows me to apologize if I dimension-jump into whatever world you’re in and vaporize myself in the genkan. I think that warrants it.
: I still don’t really understand, but...I’ll trust you if that’s what you need me to do. But know that I am incredibly broken right now and terrified that the life of my dreams is just that.
: So I apologize if I’m not as strong as I was in Aomori. Assuming you...even know how strong that was in the first place.
: I remember everything...
: You...do? But how? You-
: It’s long and complicated, but there’s an analogy involving solar panels Dad can clue you in on once we’re through here. In the meantime, we-
: Did it hurt?...
: Can I at least finish my spiel before I get into the specifics of how painful it is to vaporize an alternate version of myself?
: Sorry...what are we doing exactly? I’m still groggy and extremely nauseous, so I’m only 75%% present, but...you were talking about Ami, right?
: Right!
: Ayane, first and foremost, welcome back.
: Thank you for keeping her company while I was dying...I hope you two had fun together.
: Yeah, we’ve done a lot more than just have fun. Himawari has magical hand-powers that let her rearrange people’s memories, so we’ve been scouring the beach in search of all the girls.
: So, needless to say, it has been pretty fun.
: We’re still looking for Ami and a few of the other girls, though. So if you know something about her being involved, now is the time to say it.
: And I know the answer to this, so I am going to grade you harshly on your accuracy.
: I mean...I can’t say anything for sure, but...I’ve had some suspicions about her for a while. And the way she’s been acting with Maya lately, just...
: I feel like she knows more than she’s letting on. And that maybe she’s just pretending to be oblivious for...Ami reasons. I can’t think like a crazy person, so I can’t exactly pinpoint her motives.
: And I could be completely wrong about this. So if Hima-chan knows something, she’s much better off than I am trying to explain any of this.
: Good work, Mom. And while nothing you said was really inaccurate, you were still super vague about it, so I’m going to have to give you a B.

: Now that the cat’s out of the bag and I managed to skirt violating one more company policy by not being the one to reveal it, I’m going to go ahead and break a different policy by confirming that everything Mom said is true.
: Ami does know that time is repeating itself. And she’s concealing it from you for what I can only imagine is the same thing I said earlier. She doesn’t want to leave.
: Not being able to find her right now is par for the course too. That’s what I meant when I said she was troublesome. She always does this because she always knows when it’s coming.
: And even if we were to get ahold of her, anything we’d do to her to affect her memories would only be temporary.
: Why even bother then? If they’re just going to come back?
: Testing mostly. She’s one more thing that doesn’t make sense in what is essentially an entire world full of inconsistencies.
: We’ve figured out why Maya’s special, but Ami is a paradox of her own. And what really sucks for us is that she seems to be aware of it.
: So every time we find her, we try something new. And, once that doesn’t work, it’s back to the drawing board and time to wait for another chrono-intermission.
: What do you mean you try something new?...
: What do you do to her?...
: Me personally? Nada. A girl like Ami is way above my pay-grade. Nor am I confident that there’s anything that can really be done with her in the first place.
: We have to try, though. And I’m desperate enough to try anything at this point. So if she has some sort of answer, even if it’s a small one, I need it. It might help me save you.
: You don’t, like...hurt her...do you? Because I love you, but there’s no way I’m going to help you look for Ami if you’re going to try and torture answers out of her or something.
: I wouldn’t want to torture her either. I told you earlier — I like Ami.
: Besides, do I really look like the torturing type? I can’t even squish bugs. I have to put them in a cup and bring them outside because I’m worried they might have bug families.
: Or even worse — a bug daughter who travels through bug-time in an endless bug-effort to reunite said bug family. I don’t want to squish myself, Dad. Under...most circumstances.
: So, if we find her, then what? Because she won’t come easily if she’s avoiding you like this.
: I ask her peacefully and passively if she will divulge all of the information she possesses to me. Then I touch her head and give her a quick little temporary memory buzz.
: And when she won’t tell you anything?
: I call Shi-chan and let her take care of it.
: Shi...chan?
: My cool senpai who smokes cigarettes and refuses to tell me anything about the dark past she’s incessantly haunted by.
: Aww...you have a friend.
: Can I meet her? You never brought anyone home in Aomori. I want to make sure she’s a good influence. Which she probably isn’t since she smokes, but still.
: I was actually just about to call her and ask how-
: Ah! That’s probably her now.
